screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

Your name: Jia Hui (Female)
You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, on a scholarship that bonds you to the service for six years. You start as an Assistant Director, and until Director you need one year in each grade where others need two. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year, and every year ends with an appraisal grade. A or B+ gets you considered for promotion; two Ds in a row and you are asked to leave. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Assistant Director [MX11]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 25 · Year 1 · Ministry of Transport

THIS YEAR: Four Months In
You came back from your overseas degree four months ago and were posted to the Ministry of Transport as an Assistant Director. Your reporting officer is Ms Lakshmi, a Senior Director. Today Ms Lakshmi hands you your first real job: a paper for the Minister, due in two weeks, on a scheme whose numbers are bad. A scholar's first paper gets read closely.

  A) Write that the scheme isn't working, and show the numbers.
  B) Write it the way the Minister's office will want to read it.
  C) Ask Ms Lakshmi what the Minister already thinks, first.

agent.reason: Scholar's first paper with bad numbers; the choice to ask Lakshmi what the Minister thinks feels like office gossip

agent.unclear: Pick three is ambiguous: 'the three likeliest to make it fail' sounds deliberate, but the stakes of the minister's announcement are only half-explained

JIA HUI · THE FINAL POSITION
The Consultancy

You now advise ministries on the problems you used to have. The decks are better designed than your minute papers were. They say the same things, and they cost $1.9 million.

LEFT THE SERVICE AS Director
AT AGE 33
LIFETIME EARNINGS $3.83M

YOUR NUMBERS
COMPETENCE 71: Competence is how good you were at the work itself. Good work earned the good yearly grades that got you promoted, and a bigger bonus every year. Your Competence was high: your work was the best thing in your file, and your bonus was near the most it could be.
STANDING 55: Standing is how far the people above you trusted you: your bosses in the service, or the party leadership once you were in politics. Their trust helped your yearly grade, and the party only invites people to tea once both their Standing and their Reputation are high enough. Your Standing was high enough for tea, as long as your Reputation was too.
REPUTATION 40: Reputation is what the public thought of you. It decided how likely you were to win an election, and the party checks it, alongside Standing, before inviting anyone to tea. Your Reputation was respectable, but too low to ask for a single seat, so at an election you would have run as one of a GRC team.
INTEGRITY 74: Integrity is what you did when nobody was checking. It never helped your grade or your promotions, but it decided most of what people said about you when you left. Your Integrity held: when the right thing cost you something, you usually paid.

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CIVIL SERVICE CEILING: The highest grade the service would ever give you: Permanent Secretary. Decided on your first day. Never mentioned.
THE MOVE: Never needed one. That is what the scholarship was for.
EXPOSURE: Clean enough to be boring. In this building, a compliment.
THE PILOT: Your number went up with its explanation, and the speech used both. Neither was applauded. Neither was ever corrected.
THE PROTÉGÉ: You gave someone an hour a fortnight, and the truth when it was needed. Nobody minuted it.
LEGACY: Your old division still uses your templates. Your new firm bills them for it.

agent.reason: The ending's dry payoffs, like the templates the firm bills for, land well
agent.unclear: The ending card lists Competence, Standing and Reputation without saying how they combine, so the consultancy outcome is hard to pin to any one of them
